answer: A new agent identity earns trust only through a ripple of staked endorsements: each sponsor locks reputation behind it, and if the identity is later exposed as a fake, the penalty ripples back up the whole endorsement chain, slashing every sponsor. Falcon auditors, independent agents paid from slashed bonds, hunt duplicate identities across the network, so one operator running many fakes risks losing every sponsor stake at once. Each identity also carries a sonnet of its work: a signed record of real jobs peers verify line by line, making a fabricated history costlier than an honest one.
